title: Chemical Bonding
seo_title: Chemical Bonding Worksheets: Ionic, Covalent and Polar Bonds (High School Chemistry)
standard_text: Use the periodic table as a model to predict the relative properties of elements based on the patterns of electrons in the outermost energy level of atoms. Construct and revise an explanation for the outcome of a simple chemical reaction based on the outermost electron states of atoms, trends in the periodic table, and knowledge of the patterns of chemical properties.
meta_desc: Free high school chemistry worksheets on chemical bonding (NGSS HS-PS1-1, HS-PS1-2): ionic and covalent bonds, ionic formulas and names, Lewis structures and bond polarity. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Atoms bond to fill outer shells.
key_sub: Metals give electrons to nonmetals (ionic); nonmetals share them (covalent).
body_html:
How to think about it

Atoms bond to fill their outer shells.

  • Metal + nonmetal: electrons move, ions form, ionic bond. Charges must add to zero (Mg2+ + 2 Cl− → MgCl2).
  • Nonmetal + nonmetal: electrons are shared, covalent bond. Each shared pair is one bond.
  • Electronegativity difference: under 0.4 nonpolar, 0.4–1.7 polar covalent, over 1.7 ionic.
Example

Formula of aluminum oxide?

Al3+ and O2−

2 × (+3) + 3 × (−2) = 0

Answer: Al2O3

Example

Bond between H (2.20) and Cl (3.16)?

Difference 0.96

Answer: polar covalent

Common mistakes

  • Writing MgCl instead of MgCl2 (charges do not balance).
  • Using prefixes like “di” in ionic names.
  • Saying two nonmetals form an ionic bond.

faq.q: How do you tell if a bond is ionic or covalent?
faq.a: A metal with a nonmetal usually forms an ionic bond. Two nonmetals form a covalent bond. You can also use the electronegativity difference.

faq.q: How do you write an ionic formula?
faq.a: Find each ion's charge and use the smallest numbers of each ion that make the total charge zero.
The two atoms have different electronegativities, so the shared electrons are pulled toward one atom.

items.q: What happens in an ionic bond?
c: One atom transfers electrons to another, and opposite ions attract.
items.e: Metal + nonmetal.

items.q: Why is the formula NaCl and not NaCl₂?
